messages.subject: [statnet_help] visualization assistance
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] visualization assistance
messages.body_plain:
Hi jimi,

On 05/28/2015 10:34 AM, jimi adams wrote:
> Hi all,
> I have a data set I???ve been working with that was from a teaching
> example, and I???m trying to get a dynamic visualization of it
> configured. The basics are working, but I am trying to figure out if a
> few tweaks are possible, and I haven???t come up with anything yet, so
> any help on these would be much appreciated.
>
> 1 - As far as I can tell, tie directionality is fixed across the entire
> visualization. Is that so? I have 5 tie types (encoded as weights) some
> of which are directed, some of which are not. I???d like to allow the
> directionality to vary according to the type being visualized.

Yes, tie directionality is fixed.  However, for the purposes of 
rendering you can turn on and off the arrow based on edge type.  You 
could do this with some logic in the plot command

test<-network.initialize(3)
test[1,2]<-1
test[1,3]<-1
set.edge.attribute(test,'type',c('A','B'))
plot(test, arrowhead.cex = ifelse(test%e%'type'=='A',0,1),)

or perhaps by pre-caching an attribute for each edge to indicate if it 
should be drawn.

> 2 - I???m not figuring out how to change node color based on edge
> patterns (e.g., can someone pass something to / contract something from
> others dynamically, or should I code that outside of the visualization)?

You could probably encode some sort of edge pattern logic into plot 
commands (i.e. show vertices with degree > 2 in red) but if you have 
some sort of transmission process in mind, you will probably need to run 
a simulation ahead of time, cache a status variable on the vertices, and 
then plot that.  Have you seen the EpiModel package?  It may have a 
model that does what you want right out of the box.

best,
  -skye

messages.body_plain:
Hi Matt,

These are not errors, they are diagnostic warnings that provide additional 
information on the performance of the MCMC estimation algorithm.  You 
should still be getting results -- let me know if that's not the case.

When you see this kind of error, it suggests you might want to increase 
your MCMC.interval to reduce the correlation between draws from the chain 
(see the documentation for control.ergm).

best,
Martina

Hi Martina,

Thanks for your response!  I am not really getting results from many of the
runs that return such warnings.  I get a list of estimated coefficients,
but most have no standard deviations (NA).  I doesn't seem  like an issue
with interval length, as I am already manually setting that.  That does
raise the question:
Is there a principled or systematic way to increase the burnin, interval,
iteration control values?

Here is an example:

mod1 <-ergm(w1~edges+gwidegree(.8, fixed = T, cutoff =
30)+nodemix('smallfishsect', base = -trim.pairs)+nodecov('Resp1'),
control=control.ergm(MCMC.burnin=150000, MCMC.interval=10000,
MCMLE.maxit=35))
Iteration 1 of at most 35:
The log-likelihood improved by 1.734
Step length converged once. Increasing MCMC sample size.
Iteration 2 of at most 35:
The log-likelihood improved by 0.6029
Step length converged twice. Stopping.

This model was fit using MCMC.  To examine model diagnostics and check for
degeneracy, use the mcmc.diagnostics() function.
Warning messages:
1: In .ergm.mvar.spec0(z) :
  Excessive correlation among the statistics. Using a no-crosscorrelation
approximation.
2: In .ergm.mvar.spec0(z) :
  Excessive correlation among the statistics. Using a no-crosscorrelation
approximation.
3: In .ergm.mvar.spec0(z) :
  Excessive correlation among the statistics. Using a no-crosscorrelation
approximation.

Thanks,
Mateo

messages.body_plain:
Greetings everyone,

I am working with a bipartite network (545 Actors X 407 Events). At present, I am having trouble getting ergm to recognize the network as bipartite. When I attempt to model using ergm, I receive the following error message:

> ergm(net ~ edges + b1nodematch("district1?))
Error: The term b1nodematch does not exist for this type of ERGM. Are you sure you have the right name?


I guess that I have failed to correctly specify an option somewhere along the line. However, when I originally set the adjacency matrix ?mat? as a network object ?net', I specified the network as bipartite and it is undirected. For example, see below:

> net<-network(mat, bipartite=545)
>
> net
 Network attributes:
  vertices = 952
  directed = FALSE
  hyper = FALSE
  loops = FALSE
  multiple = FALSE
  bipartite = 545
  total edges= 2137
    missing edges= 0
    non-missing edges= 2137

 Vertex attribute names:
    vertex.names


I am just getting started with the statnet suite so this is a true beginner?s mistake. However, I was not able to identify a previous discussion on statnet_help that described a user with a similar problem. If anyone could point me in that direction, I would be very appreciative. More generally, is there a good guide or tutorial for dealing specifically with bipartite networks in statnet that anyone can recommend for a beginner?

Many thanks in advance for any help or advice you can give,


Steve Oliver

Visiting Assistant Professor
Division of Social Sciences
Yale-NUS College


________________________________

messages.body_plain:
Dear Jeff,

This did expose a bug in tergm, which will be fixed in the next release.
Other than that,

> 
> for (i in 1:10) {
> activate.network.attribute(net, "dyadic", x[i], onset=i, length=1)
> }


x is a 3D array, so x[i] will extract its i'th element. I think you're
looking for x[,,i]. Also, NAs for covariates are not allowed.

> net.fit <- stergm(net, formation= ~edges + mutual + dyadcov(net,
> "dyadic") , dissolution= ~edges + mutual  + dyadcov(net, "dyadic"),
> estimate = "CMLE", times = c(1:11))


Also, unfortunately, tergm doesn't support a series of networks with
heterogeneous sizes at this time, though it isn't explicit about it. A
full support is a complicated question, but it'll handle it more
gracefully in the next release (hopefully, next week).

                                    Pavel

messages.body_plain:
Hello Oliver,

I don?t have your data, but when I run a stripped-down version of the 
code with made-up data in the same structure as yours, the term appears 
works fine.  Since it?s a relatively new addition to our toolkit, I 
think the most likely explanation is that you have an old version of 
ergm loaded? You can find out which with sessionInfo().    I have ergm 
3.2.4 and the following code works just fine:

library(ergm)
mat <- matrix(0,952,952)
net<-network(mat, bipartite=545, directed=F)
net<- san(net~edges,target.stats=2137)
net
district1 <- sample(2:8, 952, replace=T)
set.vertex.attribute(net, "district1", district1)
myergm <- ergm(net ~ edges + b1nodematch("district1"))

My other guess was that maybe you had missing values in your district1 
attribute, and the error message was triggered by that, even if it 
pointed to a different problem.  But it appears that the attribute works 
just fine with missing data as well:

set.vertex.attribute(net, "district1", district1, v=c(1:20))
myergm <- ergm(net ~ edges + b1nodematch("district1"))

If it does turn out to be an old version, then either of the following 
should help:

update.packages(?statnet?)
update.packages(?ergm?)

Let us know if that solves the problem.

Yours,
Steve

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I feel like my question should be easy to figure out, but I just 
couldn't find any documentation on it. So let's try this mailing list:

I have a network that has a mix of directed and undirected edges. I set 
it up as a directed network, and I have no problem adding the directed 
edges. But I'm stuck at how to add the undirected ones. I tried to do 
add.edges() twice with head and tail flipped, but that produces 2 
directed edges. How can I produce a single undirected edge between 2 
vertices?

Btw, I also need to allow for multiple edges, a person could be having a 
directed edge to someone (if A says they know B) and an undirected (if C 
says that A and B know each other).

Thanks,
Andreas

messages.subject: [statnet_help] how to have both directed and undirected edges?
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] how to have both directed and undirected edges?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andreas,

"directed-ness" is a network-level property.  So if your network 
contains directed edges, all of the edges must be directed, and you will 
have to represent mutual ties with one edge in each direction as you 
suggest.

You can set a network's 'directed' attribute to FALSE, which means that 
all edges will be considered undirected.

myNet%n%'directed'<-FALSE

If you are generating a 'multiplex' network, in which there is the 
possibility of having more than one edge (of different types) you will 
probably want to set the 'multiple' property to TRUE.


 > network.initialize(50,directed = TRUE,multiple = TRUE)
  Network attributes:
   vertices = 50
   directed = TRUE
   hyper = FALSE
   loops = FALSE
   multiple = TRUE
   bipartite = FALSE
   total edges= 0
     missing edges= 0
     non-missing edges= 0

  Vertex attribute names:
     vertex.names

No edge attributes


If you need to be able to distinguish the various types of edges you 
should set some sort of type attribute on the edges as well.

best,
  -skye
